name: Resource Tutor
description_md:
### **[Bishop vs. Expert Ronan the Accuser](https://youtu.be/_JOVzwZbWyI?si=_rH_XaHxvuEfwuy9)**

### **[Complete Age of Apocalypse Expert Campaign Playthrough](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLd1L46Smijx131zr6zsxtZ0l5essBv5J5&si=0Ue8kCIH63wZQDTL)**


### Why Justice?
Bishop's alter-ego ability is one of my favorites in the game. _Temporally Displaced_ lets us grab any _Temporal_ card from the discard pile to our hand when we flip from hero to alter-ego. Half of Bishop's identity-specific cards are _Temporal_, most importantly, [Stored Energy](https://marvelcdb.com/card/45010). Every time Bishop flips to alter-ego, he can get a double resource card for free. To control threat and easily flip, I opt to play him in justice. The yellow aspect is known for its board control but can lack damage. Fortunately, Bishop has one of the highest burst damages in the game with [Super-Charged](https://marvelcdb.com/card/45006). If you guys know me, I love an amazing alter-ego ability, lots of resources, and big burst damage. Bishop has all 3!

### Easy Building

Setting up has never been so easy. Many heroes have identity-specific resource cards like Black Panther and his [Vibranium](https://marvelcdb.com/card/01044) or Captain Marvel and her [Energy Absorption](https://marvelcdb.com/card/01014), but none of them can tutor their resource card straight to their hand with just their identity's ability. Bishop can use a double resource to play an expensive card, then flip down to alter-ego, tutor [Stored Energy](https://marvelcdb.com/card/45010) to the hand and use it to play another expensive card. With this direct access to resources, we can easily set up a powerful board by playing expensive supports like [Avengers Mansion](https://marvelcdb.com/card/01091) and [The X-Jet](https://marvelcdb.com/card/32020).

### Thwart Machine
[Heroic Intuition](https://marvelcdb.com/card/01065) is key for this deck because of our access to readies. Not only can Bishop ready up with his [Concussive Blast](https://marvelcdb.com/card/45007), but this deck is loaded with 9 X-Men allies for [Utopia](https://marvelcdb.com/card/33020) to give us more readies ([Nick Fury](https://marvelcdb.com/card/01084) is the odd man out but I couldn't resist including him as one of the best resource sinks for Bishop). All of this readying allows Bishop to easily control threat.

### The Power in All of Us
We gotta add resource cards for the resource king, and I went with [The Power in All of Us](https://marvelcdb.com/card/13024) for the synergy with our basic supports and basic X-Men allies.

### Improvements
In my game against Apocalypse, I ran [Legion](https://marvelcdb.com/card/45020) and [Superpower Training](https://marvelcdb.com/card/40059), but I took them out for [Colossus](https://marvelcdb.com/card/32048) and a 2nd copy of [One Way or Another](https://marvelcdb.com/card/22015). I prefer [Colossus](https://marvelcdb.com/card/32048) as an ally for his reliable tough, while [Legion](https://marvelcdb.com/card/45020) has a wild factor of discarding the top of our deck and not knowing which effect will trigger. I also realized [Superpower Training](https://marvelcdb.com/card/40059) isn't good with Bishop because his identity-specific upgrades are either 0 cost or Temporal (so he can tutor them with his alter-ego ability). [One Way or Another](https://marvelcdb.com/card/22015) gives us more card draw to offset having a dud hand with all/no resources and Bishop can easily thwart the side scheme out.

### Hope you enjoy this decklist!
